threads.body: The comment claims the cast is safe because `T` is `Value<?>`, but for `EXTENDED_ATTRIBUTES` the application API passes `ExtendedAttributes` (see usage in LoggerTest). The cast is safe due to type erasure + converting the value to an agent `Value<?>`, but the current wording is misleading and may confuse future maintainers.

[General] createExtendedLogData() invokes setEventName(...) and setBodyValue(...) unconditionally via reflection, even though this class already has compatibility guards (canSetEventName / canUseValue) for the non-extended path. If either method is absent on older opentelemetry-sdk-testing versions, this will throw at runtime and break telemetry conversion. Consider mirroring the same guards here (and falling back to setBody(String) when Value/bodyValue isn’t available).

threads.body: [General] The PR description says this only updates the OpenTelemetry SDK to 1.63.0, but this PR also updates the Kotlin Gradle plugin / stdlib version (e.g., settings.gradle.kts now pins org.jetbrains.kotlin.jvm 2.3.21 and licenses/licenses.md reflects kotlin-stdlib 2.3.21). If intentional, the PR title/description should mention it; if not, consider reverting the Kotlin upgrade to keep the change scoped.

I guess this got removed because it was too annoying to test? I think we might need a better strategy. Maybe shading something in would help? Or perhaps allow tests to provide custom conversions for `TelemetryConverter`.
